directions/yard.md: its `## Looks` describes the frames and only one component (site-header). How yard draws listings, pricing, schedule, faq, booking and map is not stated, so the yard designs' arrangement lines were chosen from the components' own rules, not from the direction.

booking component vs businesses/rental.md: the business describes its booking as 'a request for dates: what, from when to when, how many', but the form posts one `date` and one `time` only. A rental has no field for the return day. The demo content's booking intro asks the visitor to write the return day in the message, which is a stopgap in the words, not a fix.

pricing component vs businesses/rental.md: the business asks for 'the rates: the half day, the day, the weekend, the week', which for a rental is a grid of object by duration. The component has one price per plan, so the content writes four plans (one per duration, price 'dès …') and puts each object's rate in the plan's `includes` lines. It also needs four plans where the component's advice is three.

listings component: a listing's `place` is the only free line besides the facts, and a rental has no place per object; the content uses it for where the object is collected (Dans la cour, Atelier vélos, Au comptoir). A rental's mixed stock (a van, a digger, skis) also strains the rule of the same facts in the same order: the content uses Taille, Permis, Caution, Compris for all nine.

civic.summary: A notice board people trust: a stripe of the accent across the top of the page and again at its foot, the opening one framed notice with the photograph inside it, what is on as rows that each open on a date tile, and the page closed on a solid band asking for the one thing. Large text, generous targets, plain frames.

yard.summary: An industrial site in daylight: a hazard strip over the name, heads set like stencilled bay numbers, slabs with hard ink edges, the figure of each job very large on a hazard plate, and one diagonal where the page runs out into its last slab.

launch.summary: A product's front page: one promise set large and centred over the product, which sits in a bezel like a screenshot, with the light always coming from above — a lit stretch of hairline at the top of the page glowing down behind the opening in the accent, and the same lit edge on the plan to take, the forms and the panel that closes the page. Everything else is crisp hairline panels on the page's own ground: cards in centred rows with their pictures inset, lists as tables in one panel, eyebrows as small capsules, and one action with an arrow from the first screen to the last.

atelier.summary: Work on white walls: one plate hung inside the page's margins with its label under it, the work in strict grids of numbered plates, everything that is only words an index hanging from hairlines, and the page closed by a title block ruled in the ink — no card, no tint and no accent in the chrome, so the photographs are the only loud thing.

ledger.summary: A quiet office of paper and ink: a letterhead in small capitals over a double rule, every section opened by an ink hairline and its number, its head in the margin and its entries in a narrow measure at the right, and every list ruled like a register. Wherever a label meets a figure — the opening's facts, the hours, the firm's details — a dotted leader runs to the figure at the right, as on a statement of account. No cards, no shadows, no marks under the titles.

trail.summary: The outdoors in season: one landscape edge to edge that dissolves into the page at its foot, the name set over that horizon, the dates and the ways on painted on signpost boards, the facts in a strip, and a ridge line where the page meets the ground of its footer.

points: A card with a photograph (projects, listings) is the catalogue's: square pictures and frames, what sizes it under a 2px ink rule as the hero's facts are, the listing's price in the accent.

A list (services, jobs, courses, credentials) is the carte's: a 2px ink rule over it, hairlines under the rows, the price semibold at the end. Services lose their panel and become rows in 20rem columns.
A label is the schedule's day name (small, uppercase, tracked); a figure is the display face at its weight, in the ink (process numbers are ink, not accent, as the marks are).
Testimonials keep the kit's panel, as team does, with counter's mark over each quotation and a square portrait.
Pricing names are set like carte section titles over a 2px ink rule.
Quote keeps the kit's panel, as booking does, with the form under a 2px ink rule.
Donate is a block of the second ground with no edge, as the hours strip is.
Ten titles take the heading size; credentials-title is a carte section label instead, since the kit sets it small on purpose.
Things the caller should know:

The featured pricing plan keeps the kit's accent ring. I first edged it in 1.5px ink like the map, but in marigold, whose panels are already edged in ink with a hard shadow, the featured plan came out fainter than the plans beside it, so I removed that rule.

Rules that change a `display` or drop a component's own rule are scoped to `:not([data-variant])`: the services row grid, the pricing head rule, the credentials list rule and the quote form rule. An arrangement therefore starts from the component's own markup. ArrangementTest rejects any direction rule that names a variant value, so `:not([data-variant='split'])` was not possible; the quote's `plain` arrangement draws no ink rule over its form as a result.

Projects and listings stay in the kit's grid rather than counter's rail, because the `rows`, `index` and `feature` arrangements assume a grid. Square photographs make a single-column stack tall: in a third of board, three listings run about 1900px.
Not seen in a picture: the testimonial's square portrait (the specimens carry no portraits) and credentials with logos. Those rules are a border-radius and nothing else.
Arrangements (`data-variant`) were not photographed, because the specimens carry none; how the rules sit under them is reasoned from the arrangement CSS only.
How market now draws them:
Titles: all eleven `*-title` parts take `--heading-size` and `--heading-leading`, credentials included.
Glass cards: projects, services, testimonials, pricing plans, listings, quote and donate get market's glass (soft rule edge, raise at 72%, no shadow, backdrop blur).
Glass where the markup draws rules: process steps, credentials items, and the jobs and courses lists, each list one panel with 1.5rem in, as the agenda's.
Photographs: projects and listings have the photograph or frame inset 1rem on `--radius-media`, as the catalogue's.
Labels: the projects' place and year is the eyebrow's pill with its highlight dot; the jobs' facts are pills on the same tint.
States: the pricing flag, listings status and courses seats keep the markup's colours and become pills.
Prices: services, listings and courses prices are semibold; the service's and listing's sit at the end, as the catalogue's. The listing's price moves from the display face to `var(--font-body)`.
Services: laid out as the catalogue's row, with the icon on a tinted square at the left, at 20rem columns.
Dots: a highlight dot comes before the process duration and the quote and donate notes, and opens each testimonial.
Decisions to know about:

Variant scoping: the rules that replace the markup's own edges or layout (process steps, credentials items, the jobs and courses panels, the services row, the donate account block) apply only under `:not([data-variant])`.

Featured plan: the glass's `box-shadow: none` removes the markup's accent ring, so the rules redraw it as an accent border plus a 1px accent shadow. The plan is found by `:has([data-kit-part='pricing-flag'], .btn-primary)`; a featured plan with neither a flag nor a link is drawn like the others.
Courses seats: "Complet" and "3 places" share one hook, so only the shape changes and the colours stay the markup's.
Lists' padding: 1.5rem all round, matching the existing `events-list` exactly; a tighter top looked slightly better but differed from the agenda beside it.
Donate account: it stands on the band's 16% highlight tint with its labels set to the ink, through `[data-kit-part='donate-detail'] > :first-child`.
Left alone: `--section-gap` (a title sits 1.25rem under the previous section's cards, as the menu and team titles already do) and the display-face figures (pricing price, projects figure).
What studio now does:
Heads: ten titles take the section size and are centred with their intros. credentials-title is deliberately not a section head: it is a small tracked label, centred.
Photo cards (projects, listings): no panel, 3/4, square corners, three across at most, as the catalogue's tiles.
Names: small, uppercase, tracked 0.2em in the body face at 600, the way features-item-title and menu-section-title are written.
Prices and durations: display face, as menu-price.

Flags, chips and ticks: the listing's status, the plan's flag, the jobs' facts and the courses' seats become quiet tracked labels; the pricing ticks are hidden; icons and arrows are in the ink, not the accent.
Panels: quote keeps its panel as booking does; donate loses it and becomes a 40rem centred column like the schedule.
Things to know:

A direction rule may not name an arrangement's word: the arrangement test fails any `[data-variant='…']` selector that carries `data-direction`. So the rules only step aside with `:not([data-variant])`. Two consequences: projects' `index` arrangement has no hairlines between its rows in studio (the panel edge it relied on is gone), and the quote's copy is centred in every arrangement, `split` included, as booking-title already is.
Arranged services (`rows`, `tiles`) keep a hairline box on nothing instead of losing their edge, so `rows` still reads as ruled.
A featured plan is found by `:has(.btn-primary, [data-kit-part='pricing-flag'])`; a featured plan with neither a link nor a flag gets the plain hairline.
The plan's flag and the listing's status sit on `--color-canvas`, so they assume the page's ground behind them.

Existing studio draws catalogue-name and team-name in the display face, because the base `h3` rule gives it and those rules set no family. My card names are in the body face, so a listing's name and a catalogue's name differ in face though both are small tracked capitals. Say if you want them matched to the catalogue instead.
jobs-name and courses-name only take `font-weight: 400`, mirroring events-name, so all three rows render the same.

In the journal specimen of set a, the second project's photograph did not paint in two takes (the tile kept its space); the same image painted in marketing and carte. I did not find the cause; the markup is identical and none of my rules hides an image.
Catalogue family (projects, listings): no panel edge or surface, pictures on --radius-media at the markup's own 4/3, a card with a link lifts 4px as the doors do.
Carte family (services, jobs, courses): 44rem and centred, hairlines between rows. Courses' date column lines up with events'.
Team family (testimonials): no card, quotation and name in the display face, portrait a small 4/5 plate.
Map family (pricing plans, quote, donate): hairline panel on --radius-media, no shadow. The featured plan and donate carry the accent's glow that the photo-less hero already uses.
Process keeps the kit's grid under hairlines; credentials is a strip between two hairlines.
Decisions worth knowing:

Ten titles take --heading-size. credentials-title does not: its markup is text-lg, so hearth sets it as a small uppercase tracked label over the strip. If it should be a section head, add it to the first rule and drop the label rule.

The kit's ArrangementTest treats any selector containing [data-variant='…'] as an arrangement, so a direction can only step aside with :not([data-variant]). All layout rules are scoped that way; the un-panelling is unscoped, as hearth's catalogue and team already are. Consequence: in projects 'index' and services 'rows' the rows lose the panel edge that ruled them, and I could not add a hairline for those words. Not verified in pictures:
No arrangement (variant) was photographed; the specimens draw only the default.
The specimens carry no testimonial portrait and no credential logo, so the 3rem by 3.75rem portrait rule is unseen. Logos are untouched, and a dark logo on this pinned-dark page would be hard to see.
In sandstone and plum the display face is loaded only at 600/700, so the quotations render semibold; in vellum and ember they are regular.

Round 1 marketing/sandstone, round 2 split/vellum (set a) and journal/plum (set b), round 3 after the last change: marketing/ember full pages (the two shots returned) plus sandstone at 390px wide. A listing photograph is blank in a few shots (b2 and the 390px shots); the blank one changes from shot to shot, so I read it as the specimen's lazy-loaded images, not a rule.
